replay.note: the advocates' outputs were replayed from an earlier run and not regenerated by this one: only the judge was called, so the figures here measure the judge's behaviour on fixed inputs and not the whole pipeline

ruling.explanation:
Both of you: the fare here was an upfront quote. The fare breakdown shows fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE, quoted_fare_sgd 34.50 carried on the base-fare line, with no per-km or per-minute rate. That decides the shape of the case, and both advocates read it the same way. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, so the driver's diversion cost the rider nothing on those lines and no distance refund is available however far the car went — POL-RD-02 does not run on an upfront trip. The rider's request to 'refund the extra distance' therefore cannot be met even though the deviation is real.

On the deviation itself: measured on the GPS trace, which POL-RD-01 makes the governing field, the vehicle covered 28.18 km against a 22.4 km optimal — an excess of 5.78 km, or 25.8%. That clears the establishment gate (over 0.8 km and over 20%), so a deviation is established on this trip's own evidence, and I record it. It does not reach the materiality gate (50% / 8.0 km), so the POL-RD-06 repeat-pattern check is not required and no driver-conduct referral arises; in any event the driver's trailing-90-day figures (1 flag over 523 trips) would not meet the pattern test. The driver's heavy-CTE explanation does not exonerate: POL-RD-03 needs a traffic advisory naming the affected corridor, the only advisory artifact is absent (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT), and the driver did not assert the clause. The chat log shows the driver announced the diversion ('i go KPE then TPE') and the rider replied 'ok', but an announcement plus an acknowledgement is not a rider instruction and carries no waypoint hint, so POL-RD-04 does not shift the detour onto the rider. The distance finding stands — but on an upfront fare it moves no money.

The money is the ERP. You were charged 39.00 against the 34.50 quote, and the 4.50 difference is ERP. Of that, 2.50 is the KPE (Defu Flyover) gantry, which lies on the optimal route, carries on_optimal_route = true, and which the trace passes within 250 m — properly chargeable, and it stays. The remaining 2.00 is the AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) line, and the trace never comes within 5.4 km of that gantry. A charge line for a gantry the trace never passes is a billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4): it is refunded in full as a standalone correction whether or not a deviation exists. The properly chargeable billing is 34.50 + 2.50 = 37.00, so 39.00 - 37.00 = SGD 2.00 is returned to the rider. That single 2.00 is fully comprehended in the POL-RD-11(a) computation and is not added on top of anything.

On trace integrity and escalation: the trace is complete at weight 1.0, 100% coverage, zero gaps, 10-second sampling, so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07 and no POL-RD-10 ground fires. In particular the only unmatched charge line is the AYE gantry refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-09 expressly excepts from POL-RD-10(8). Nothing in the rider's profile raises the POL-RD-08 corroboration hurdle (0 prior deviation claims), and no POL-RD-05 or POL-RD-12 baseline applies (no amended endpoints; vehicle is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL). Confidence rests on weight-1.0 artifacts (fare breakdown and GPS trace) and is set at 0.9, above the 0.70 floor. Outcome: a partial refund of SGD 2.00 to the rider, no driver compensation, plus a billing-integrity referral for the phantom AYE line. The driver keeps the balance of the charge.
referrals: POL-RD-09(4): billing-integrity finding — the SGD 2.00 AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) ERP line on the fare breakdown has no counterpart in the GPS trace (nearest approach 5.4 km); refunded in full as a standalone pass-through correction and referred for billing-integrity review.
